checks.scenario: Isolated node:test domain checks for exact calendar preservation, optional absence, real-calendar parsing, task isolation, and controlled demonstrator boundary responses; not product decisions on unresolved policies.
Syntax-check declared JavaScript/MJS, validate fixed assets/import references and package scripts; no HTTP/browser verification or production bundle claim.

AC-001.reason: Planned exact calendar preservation through domain state and application interface; unit/build evidence only here, independent QA verifies end-to-end behavior.

AC-002.reason: Planned optional date representation and undated UI; unit assertions, with independent QA acceptance evidence required later.

FR-001.reason: Planned domain, HTTP adapter and UI for initial exact future-calendar-date assignment only.

FR-002.reason: Planned nullable date state and undated display; no clearing capability.

FR-003.reason: Past-date behavior remains deferred; demonstration unimplemented-path reporting is not a product acceptance/rejection rule.

tasks.description: Prepare dependency-free Node package scripts, unit/build check runner and local run instructions. No package installation.
Implement strict calendar parsing, seeded in-memory task repository and initial-assignment domain operations together with isolated unit tests.
Implement loopback HTTP and fixed static-asset adapters with bounded JSON, controlled errors, same-origin mutation and response headers. No QA integration automation.
Implement plain browser UI for undated tasks and initial future-date assignment, exact date display and safe text rendering. No QA/browser automation.
Complete syntax/assets/import checks and run named unit/build checks through the orchestrator; present actual source changes and task evidence for separate human code review.

unresolved.text: Whether past due dates may be selected remains deferred pending consultation with support.
Past-date policy remains deferred; neither business acceptance nor business rejection is selected.
Past-date assignment remains blocked and outside the executable product acceptance scope.
Changing or clearing an already assigned due date remains undefined; no such functional capability is introduced.
